result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_nodes()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add multiple nodes to the graph in a single call. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L824-L936){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_nodes( nodes, type=None, **shared_attrs, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Add several nodes](/assets/graphs/add-nodes.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: a four-node cycle A, B, D, C. After: two new nodes, E and F, appear in the accent color beside it in one call, with no edges; nothing else changes." width="100%"} A bulk version of `add_node()` that accepts a list of node labels and applies shared attributes to all of them. Individual nodes can override shared attributes by passing a tuple of `(label, dict)` instead of a bare label. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[list, range]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node labels to add. Each element can be: - A string or int label (e.g., `'Alice'`, `42`). - A tuple of `(label, attrs_dict)` to override shared attributes for that node. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional type applied to every node (unless overridden per-node). [**shared_attrs]{.doc-parameter-name} : Attributes applied to every node (unless overridden per-node). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns self to enable method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Add several nodes at once with a shared type: ::: {#7a303b79 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes( ['Alice', 'Bob', 'Carol'], type='person' ) graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Number of nodes : 3 Number of edges : 0 Directed : False Density : 0.00 Average degree (min, max) : 0.00 (0, 0) Connected : False Number of connected components : 3 Tree : False Bipartite : True ``` ::: ::: Per-node overrides via tuples: ::: {#640788eb .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes( [ 'Alice', ('Bob', {'role': 'admin'}), 'Carol', ], type='person' ) graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` Number of nodes : 3 Number of edges : 0 Directed : False Density : 0.00 Average degree (min, max) : 0.00 (0, 0) Connected : False Number of connected components : 3 Tree : False Bipartite : True ``` ::: ::: Chaining with other methods: ::: {#6fce25b6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes( ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'], type='router' ) .add_edges([('A', 'B'), ('B', 'C'), ('C', 'D')]) ) graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Number of nodes : 4 Number of edges : 3 Directed : True Density : 0.25 Average degree (min, max) : 1.50 (1, 2) Strongly connected : False Weakly connected : True Number of strongly connected components : 4 Number of weakly connected components : 1 ``` ::: ::: Use a range for numeric node labels: ::: {#9d70872c .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(range(1, 6)) graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Number of nodes : 5 Number of edges : 0 Directed : False Density : 0.00 Average degree (min, max) : 0.00 (0, 0) Connected : False Number of connected components : 5 Tree : False Bipartite : True ``` ::: :::
